Broadcast Systems Integration Brief

Avid Technology

The dominant platform for NLE, production asset management, and newsroom computer systems in tier-1 broadcast. MediaCentral is the integration hub; everything else connects through it.

NLE PAM / MAM NRCS MOS 2.8.5 / 3.0 AAF / OMF REST API

Platform Overview

Avid's product stack is built around the MediaCentral Platform — a microservices-based middleware layer that abstracts access to Media Composer (NLE), Interplay Production (PAM), iNEWS (NRCS), and shared storage. Third-party systems integrate via the MediaCentral REST API (v1/v2) rather than directly into individual applications. Understanding this architectural pattern is the prerequisite for any Avid integration project.

Primary API
REST v2 + SOAP (legacy)
NRCS Protocol
MOS 2.8.5 / 3.0
NLE Interchange
AAF, OMF, MXF OP-Atom
Auth
OAuth 2.0 (MC Platform)
Cloud
Nexis | CloudSpaces
Monitoring
SNMP v2c, syslog

Product Integration Briefs

Each card covers the integration interface, protocol stack, and known engineering constraints.

Media Operations Platform

MediaCentral | Cloud UX

Browser-based production platform that aggregates Avid and third-party systems through the MediaCentral Services layer. Replaces the legacy MediaCentral | UX desktop client.

Architecture
Microservices on Kubernetes. Each service (Search, Assets, Collaborate) runs independently and connects to MediaCentral Bus via AMQP messaging.
APIs
REST v2 WebSocket OAuth 2.0 — all third-party connectors (Dalet, EVS, Ross) integrate via MC REST v2, not direct database access.
Cloud Deploy
AWS and Azure validated via Avid Nexis | CloudSpaces. On-prem Nexis CIFS/NFS volumes are mounted as cloud-tier storage bridges. Bandwidth requirement: 10 Gbps minimum for proxy workflows.
AI Features
MediaCentral | AI (speech-to-text, auto-tagging) adds metadata via REST API back to the MediaCentral index. Runs as a separate licensed service — not bundled with base UX.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownMC Bus service discovery breaks on multi-NIC hosts if the primary NIC is not correctly configured in avid-service-registry.yml. Avid support frequently under-documents NIC binding requirements for containerised deployments.
Production Asset Management

Interplay | Production (PAM)

Server-based PAM that manages MXF media assets on Avid Nexis shared storage. Exposes a Windows COM/DCOM API (legacy) and a REST gateway layer introduced in v3.7+.

Architecture
Windows Server 2019/2022 required for Interplay Engine. No Linux deployment supported as of 2026. Database: Microsoft SQL Server (bundled version — not replaceable).
APIs
REST v1 (gateway) COM/DCOM (legacy) AAF SDK — External MAMs (Dalet, Grass Valley STRATUS) connect via the REST gateway. Direct COM access requires Windows-side connector service.
Media Format
MXF OP-Atom (audio and video in separate files). AAF composition references these atoms. Non-Avid systems reading AAF must resolve MXF atom paths via UNC share — ensure consistent share naming across all workstations.
Cloud Hybrid
Interplay Engine cannot run in cloud; only the MediaCentral REST gateway can be cloud-hosted. Full cloud Interplay requires migration to cloud-native MediaCentral | Asset Management (separate product and licence).
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownInterplay checkin/checkout locks are held at the database row level. Third-party connectors that do not explicitly release locks after failed transactions will leave assets in a permanently locked state requiring direct SQL intervention.
Cloud-Native Asset Management

MediaCentral | Asset Management

Cloud-native successor to Interplay Production. Object-storage backend (S3-compatible) with a GraphQL API replacing the legacy COM/DCOM interface. Currently coexists with Interplay in hybrid deployments.

Architecture
Containerised microservices on Kubernetes. Asset metadata stored in Elasticsearch; essence in S3-compatible object storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob, or on-prem MinIO).
APIs
GraphQL REST v2 Webhooks — GraphQL schema exposes asset lifecycle events (ingest, version, archive) for real-time third-party integration.
AI Integration
Native connectors for AWS Rekognition and Google Video AI for face recognition and scene classification. Output written to Elasticsearch metadata index. Requires separate Avid AI Services licence.
⚠ Integration Risk
MigrationMigrating from Interplay Production requires running both systems in parallel for 3–6 months. Asset GUID mapping between Interplay's SQL schema and MCAM's Elasticsearch index is not automatic — requires custom ETL pipeline.
Newsroom Computer System (NRCS)

Avid iNEWS

The broadcast industry's dominant NRCS, used by the majority of tier-1 and tier-2 news broadcasters globally. Story-centric architecture where rundowns, scripts, and media assignments are the primary data objects.

Architecture
iNEWS Server runs on Windows Server. Custom proprietary file system (iNEWS FTP) exposes story queues as a filesystem hierarchy. No direct REST API on the iNEWS Server — REST access goes through MediaCentral.
Protocols
MOS 2.8.5 MOS 3.0 iNEWS FTP NRCS WebSocket (MC) — Graphics systems (Vizrt, Chyron, Ross) connect via MOS 2.8.5 or 3.0. MOS 3.0 adds runorder sync and direct story-to-graphics binding.
MOS Integration
MOS gateway configuration requires matching MOS client IDs between iNEWS and the graphics/playout system. ID mismatches are the most common integration failure — validate with Avid's MOS configuration diagnostic tool before go-live.
AI Features
Avid AI Marketplace connectors provide script auto-suggest, archive search, and caption generation into iNEWS story fields. Delivered via MediaCentral App Framework — not native to iNEWS Server.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnowniNEWS FTP port (21 plain text) is frequently blocked by facility security policies. Integrations that write to iNEWS queues directly (automation systems, AP wire) require explicit firewall rule and iNEWS FTP user configuration — not documented in the default integration guides.
Production Management

Avid Media Composer

The NLE underpinning Avid's production stack. In networked environments it operates as a client of MediaCentral, checking in and out MXF media from Nexis shared storage rather than accessing local disk.

Architecture
Desktop client (Windows / macOS). In Avid Everywhere configuration, Media Composer communicates with Interplay Production Engine via Interplay Client Services (TCP 8321). All asset operations go through the engine — not direct disk access.
Interchange
AAF OMF MXF OP-Atom EDL — AAF with embedded media is used for interchange with DaVinci Resolve and Flame. AAF composition-only (no embedded media) requires matching Nexis mount points on the receiving system.
AI Features
ScriptSync (phoneme-based speech alignment for transcript-based editing). SpeakersID (face/voice identification with third-party transcription service). Both require MediaCentral AI Services licence.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownMedia Composer version must match Interplay Client Services version within a two-release window. Upgrading Media Composer before upgrading Interplay Engine breaks checkout/checkin operations silently — no error dialogue, assets simply fail to check out.
